q_en: Which small words change the ending of the words after them?
q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ صَغِيرَةٍ تُغَيِّرُ آخِرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا؟
not_yet: أَنْ before a verb (“to”): Lesson 69. Here only أَنَّ + a noun.
The sisters of كَانَ with a verb as the statement: later.
Every ending of every kind of noun: here only ـُ ـَ ـًا ـٌ.
not_yet_ar: «أَنْ» قَبْلَ الْفِعْلِ: فِي الدَّرْسِ ٦٩. هُنَا «أَنَّ» مَعَ الِاسْمِ فَقَطْ.
أَخَوَاتُ كَانَ مَعَ خَبَرٍ هُوَ فِعْلٌ: لَاحِقًا.
كُلُّ أَوَاخِرِ الْأَسْمَاءِ: هُنَا ـُ وَـَ وَـًا وَـٌ فَقَطْ.

slides.head_en: Look: one sentence, four small words
slides.head_ar: اُنْظُرْ: جُمْلَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ وَأَرْبَعُ كَلِمَاتٍ صَغِيرَةٍ

lines: What ending does the last word have each time?
مَا آخِرُ الْكَلِمَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ كُلَّ مَرَّةٍ؟
What does each first word add to the meaning?
مَاذَا تَزِيدُ كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ أُولَى عَلَى الْمَعْنَى؟
Compare لَكِنْ and لَكِنَّ: which changes the next word?
قَارِنْ بَيْنَ «لَكِنْ» وَ«لَكِنَّ»: أَيُّهُمَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بَعْدَهُ؟

cards.def_en: The topic keeps ـُ. The statement takes ـًا.
The topic takes ـَ. The statement keeps ـُ.
Topic and statement: both end in ـُ until a small word comes in front.

slides.note: Each one leaves the topic alone and puts the statement in ـًا (ـَ, ـًا, ـَةً).
slides.note_ar: كُلٌّ مِنْهَا يَتْرُكُ الْمُبْتَدَأَ مَرْفُوعًا وَيَجْعَلُ الْخَبَرَ مَنْصُوبًا.

sents: The boy is small, but his knowledge is much.
As if the mosque were a big house.
If only the lesson were short.
Perhaps the Habib is in the ribāṭ.

slides.note: Each one puts the topic in ـَ and leaves the statement in ـٌ.
slides.note_ar: كُلٌّ مِنْهَا يَنْصِبُ الْمُبْتَدَأَ وَيَتْرُكُ الْخَبَرَ مَرْفُوعًا.

slides.head_en: The same sentence in the two families
rows: If only the lesson were easy.
As if the water were cold.
slides.note: Left: topic ـُ, statement ـًا. Right: topic ـَ, statement ـٌ.
slides.note_ar: يَسَارًا: الْمُبْتَدَأُ ـُ وَالْخَبَرُ ـًا. يَمِينًا: الْمُبْتَدَأُ ـَ وَالْخَبَرُ ـٌ.

slides.note: They work like the first word of an iḍāfa (“of”): the noun after them takes ـِ.
slides.note_ar: هُمَا كَأَوَّلِ كَلِمَةٍ فِي الْإِضَافَةِ: الِاسْمُ بَعْدَهُمَا مَجْرُورٌ.

slides.head_en: Try: what does it mean, and what ending follows?
items: The boy became sad (in the evening) · statement ـًا
Perhaps the mosque is near · topic ـَ

slides.why: Wrong! لَيْتَ is a sister of إِنَّ: the topic takes ـَ. Say: لَيْتَ الْوَلَدَ سَعِيدٌ.
slides.why_ar: هَذَا خَطَأٌ! «لَيْتَ» مِنْ أَخَوَاتِ إِنَّ، فَالْمُبْتَدَأُ بَعْدَهَا مَنْصُوبٌ: لَيْتَ الْوَلَدَ سَعِيدٌ.

lines: وَأَصْلُ الْإِيمَانِ: أَنْ تَعْتَقِدَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى مَوْجُودٌ، وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى وَاحِدٌ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَلَا مِثْلَ لَهُ، وَلَا شِبْهَ لَهُ
The root of faith: that you believe that God Most High exists, and that He is One, with no partner, no equal and no likeness.
وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى بَعَثَ سَيِّدَنَا مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدَهُ وَرَسُولَهُ إِلَى جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ
And that He, Most High, sent our master Muḥammad ﷺ, His servant and messenger, to all creation.
وَأَنَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ صَادِقٌ فِي جَمِيعِ مَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ عَنِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
And that he, upon him be blessings and peace, is truthful in all that he reported from God Most High.
وَأَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ وَجَمِيعَ كُتُبِ اللَّهِ الْمُنَزَّلَةِ حَقٌّ، وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ حَقٌّ، وَالْجَنَّةُ حَقٌّ، وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ
And that the Qur’an and all the books God sent down are true, the angels are true, Paradise is true and the Fire is true.
slides.source: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa of Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī (1069–1145 AH)

lines: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلهِ ، وَالْعَظَمَةُ وَالسُّلْطَانُ لِلهِ ، وَالْعِزَّةُ وَالْقُدْرَةُ لِلهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
We have entered the morning, and the kingdom has entered the morning, belonging to God; majesty and sovereignty are God’s; might and power are God’s, Lord of the worlds.
أَصْبَحْنَا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ ، وَعَلَى كَلِمَةِ الْإِخْلَاصِ
We have entered the morning on the natural way of Islam and on the word of sincerity.
فَأَبْشِرْ ؛ فَإِنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَبْسُطُ لَكَ أَجْنِحَتَهَا إِذَا مَشَيْتَ
Rejoice! For the angels spread their wings for you when you walk.
and by His favour you became brothers.
slides.source: the Qur’an, sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:103 (the middle of the verse)

lines: كَانَ ثَوَابُهُ عَلَى اللهِ، وَكَانَ مُنْقَلَبُهُ إِلَى رِضْوَانِ اللهِ وَجَنَّتِهِ
His reward was with God, and his return was to God’s good pleasure and His Garden.
slides.source: Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād

lines: كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
Thus God makes His signs clear to you, so that you may be guided.
slides.source: the Qur’an, sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:103 (the end of the verse)

أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ «قَبْلَ» وَ«بَعْدَ» مَعَ الِاسْمِ بَعْدَهُمَا.

items.en: ★ The word جَمِيع ends in ـِ in line 2 and in ـَ in line 4. Why?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا آخِرُ «جَمِيع» ـِ فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ وَـَ فِي السَّطْرِ ٤؟
items.model: Line 2: it follows إِلَى (a preposition), so ـِ. Line 4: it is joined to الْقُرْآنَ, which follows أَنَّ, so ـَ.

items.en: ★ What do اللهَ (line 1) and الْقُرْآنَ (line 4) have in common after أَنَّ?
items.model: Both end in ـَ: أَنَّ is a sister of إِنَّ and puts the topic in ـَ.

sections.name: C
sections.en: A short story: the evening in the ribāṭ. Read it, then answer.
lines: كَانَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ قَبْلَ الرَّاتِبِ.
Ahmad was in the ribāṭ before the Rātib.
In the evening the mosque was open to the people.
بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ جَلَسَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
After the Rātib the Habib sat in the circle.
Ahmad said: If only the majlis were long.
لَكِنَّ الْوَقْتَ قَصِيرٌ، وَمَا زَالَ الطُّلَّابُ جَالِسِينَ.
But the time is short, and the students are still sitting.
Perhaps the Habib will hear the question.
صَارَ أَحْمَدُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ الْحَبِيبَ سَمِعَ السُّؤَالَ.
Ahmad became happy because the Habib heard the question.
As if the mosque were the house of knowledge.

Words for the last rows: يُبَيِّنُ = he makes clear · ءَايَٰتِهِ = His signs · تَهْتَدُونَ = you are guided · فِطْرَة = the natural way · الْإِخْلَاص = sincerity · أَبْشِرْ = rejoice! · الْمَلَائِكَة = the angels · تَبْسُطُ = they spread · أَجْنِحَتَهَا = their wings

items.model: The boy became happy after the lesson.

items.ar: مَا زَالَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ.
items.model: The students are still in the mosque after the Rātib.

items.ar: لَعَلَّ الْحَبِيبَ يَجْلِسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ.
items.model: Perhaps the Habib will sit in the circle after the prayer.
The house is far, but the ribāṭ is near.
As if the muṣḥaf were a light in the mosque.
The guests were happy in the ribāṭ that evening.

items.ar: لَيْسَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا لَكِنَّ الْوَقْتَ قَصِيرٌ.
items.model: The lesson is not difficult, but the time is short.
The students are still remembering God.
Ahmad was a student and became a teacher.

items.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
items.model: Thus God makes His signs clear to you, so that you may be guided.

items.ar: أَصْبَحْنَا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ ، وَعَلَى كَلِمَةِ الْإِخْلَاصِ  فَأَبْشِرْ ؛ فَإِنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَبْسُطُ لَكَ أَجْنِحَتَهَا إِذَا مَشَيْتَ
items.model: We have entered the morning on the natural way of Islam and on the word of sincerity. Rejoice! For the angels spread their wings for you when you walk.
The student became a teacher in the school.

sections.name: AC
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–100
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
